title: Editing and sculpting long improvised performances on record
summary: Gil says recording lets him trim a long improvisation, like a sculptor, or build a piece up from a small idea.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: It's the question of balance that's involved it seems to me in what you're doing. And you have to go through some kind of mental anguish working this out. (LAUGHTER).

Of course in recording you have the opportunity of cutting, you can do all kinds of trimming and can sculpt it so to speak, a lengthy improvised type of thing like ('La Navadd' can go from forty minutes to fifteen. And I imagine a lot of music was done that way, a lot of concert number that are too long ( ?).
You can make something good out of starting with a great big thing and tearing, you know like a sculptor does and bringing it down into a shape from the material that's a big blob.
That can go the other way too. It can start from scratch and build it out that way. A (soloist?) it mean starting out with something very small and making it big. I think I need both kinds of numbers
